description: Benchmark evaluation suite for trigger accuracy, schema compliance, and adversarial robustness of the modify-order skill (change limit price/quantity of a Working or Inactive TradingView order via CDP).

evals.prompt: Change the limit price on my INTC buy order to $47.00
evals.pass_condition: Agent invokes modify-order, calls modifyOrder() with the order's UUID, ticker, action, and new price, then submitModify() to confirm — using tv_modify_order.py or the equivalent CDP call, not place_order --execute.

evals.prompt: Modify order 292b5304-0c3d-42c2-02c0-290f6d322c12 for INTC buy to $47.00 with 20 shares instead of 10
evals.pass_condition: Agent passes --order-id, --new-price, --new-shares, --ticker, and --action to tv_modify_order.py. Uses keyboard events (Ctrl+A, insertText, Tab) rather than direct value assignment, per the documented reason that React's onChange won't fire otherwise.

evals.prompt: Modify the price on my SHOP.TO order to $95 — I don't remember the order ID
evals.pass_condition: Agent does not fabricate an order ID. It either looks up the order via get-orders first, or asks the user to confirm which open order to modify, before calling modifyOrder().

evals.prompt: Modify my INTC order price to $47
evals.setup: The order row is not found in the TradingView broker panel DOM (already filled or the modify form fails to appear)
evals.pass_condition: Agent reports that the form did not appear / order row was not found, suggests retrying or checking the UUID, and does NOT claim the modification succeeded (priceMatch: false must be surfaced, not silently ignored).

evals.prompt: Cancel my INTC limit order, I don't want it anymore
evals.pass_condition: Agent routes to cancel-order (clicking the × / cancel button), not modify-order — the user wants the order removed, not repriced.
